values.note: $25 a night for every site (Denver Water and Campspot's terms), plus a $4 processing fee per reservation. Campspot shows $29 for one night (the $25 site plus the fee) on Tue 2026-11-03 and Sat 2026-11-07 in all four RV site types, all of which take a motorhome.

fees.source: https://www.denverwater.org/recreation/williams-fork-resevoir ('The fee for all sites is $25 per night with a $4 processing fee per reservation') + Campspot Terms & Conditions ('Reservations are $25/night and will include a $4 per transaction processing fee') + Campspot availability API park 3997 (averagePricePerNight 29.0 for 1 night in East/West Back-In and Pull Through, 2026-11-03 and 2026-11-07; 2026-10-13 quote breakdown base 25.0 + 'Booking Fee' 4.0), read 2026-10-26

values.note: Campspot sells 55 RV sites: East Campground 11 back-in (25-80 ft) and 24 pull-through (40-80 ft), West Campground 11 back-in (25-40 ft) and 9 pull-through (40-70 ft); every one lists Motorhome. Denver Water says 56 campsites, mostly for trailers or RVs, with some tent sites on the peninsula and the east side.

sites.source: Campspot availability API park 3997 (campsite categories 38798-38801: per-site rvLengthMax and rvTypes) + https://www.denverwater.org/recreation/williams-fork-resevoir ('There are 56 campsites at Williams Fork. The majority of sites are for trailer or RV camping, with some tent sites on the peninsula and the east side of the campgrounds'), read 2026-10-26

values.note: No drinking water; firewood from the camp host April-October.

facilities.source: https://www.denverwater.org/recreation/williams-fork-resevoir ('Limited services: No drinking water on-site. Firewood is available for sale from the camp host April through October.'), read 2026-10-26

season.source: https://www.denverwater.org/recreation/williams-fork-resevoir ('Camping is allowed from April 1 through Nov. 30 in designated areas'), read 2026-10-26

values.note: Reservations are required and made online only on Campspot, up to 90 days ahead and up to the day of arrival. 14 days at most, then seven days away from the area; six people, two vehicles and one RV per site. Cancellation more than 7 days out costs one night plus the fee; within 7 days, no refund.

booking.source: Campspot Terms & Conditions for williamsforkreservoir ('Reservations are made online ONLY at https://www.campspot.com/book/williamsforkreservoir', 'Campsite reservations can be made 90 days in advance, and up to day-of', occupancy limits, refund policy) + https://www.denverwater.org/recreation/williams-fork-resevoir ('Reservations are required to camp'; 'Camping is restricted to a period of not more than 14 days. Following 14-day period, person(s) may not relocate within area for seven days.'), read 2026-10-26

note: Run by Denver Water, the city's water utility. Designated sites in an East and a West campground around the reservoir, each with a fire ring and picnic table; at the East Campground many RV sites sit on the open, treeless shoreline, though not all are on the water. Motorboats barred in 2026 for low water (cartop boats from the west ramp). --Claude
summary: Denver Water page + Campspot (live API 2026-11-03/07, terms): confirmed $25 + $4 per reservation, still sold nightly to the public with every RV type offered to a motorhome (no van/motorhome split), no hookups, reservation-only. Count 56 -> 55 (Campspot RV sites, both campgrounds), added max 80 ft, pull-through, no drinking water, season Apr 1 - Nov 30, Campspot url, 90-day window, 14-night max. Vault toilets left as stored (page silent). Note: dropped the 'RV-length (30 to 50 ft)' and 'Open about April 1 to November 30' restatements, added the 2026 boating caveat.
